resources.string: Lille will open X and wait — you log in yourself, in her browser, then hand back. She never sees your password.
Lille is free. She runs on your Fluid name.
Type your Fluid username, connect your Fluid wallet, and Lille opens — the connected wallet must be the one that owns the name. No password, no API key: your Fluid name is your login.
Invited by a friend? Their Lille name (optional)
1. Copy the code below.\n2. Open Fluid → More → WalletConnect.\n3. Paste the code and approve.
Waiting for your approval in Fluid…
New to Fluid? Get Fluid and create your name

Or open Fluid right here, inside Lille — the code is copied for you; in Fluid tap More → WalletConnect, paste, approve. First time on this embedded browser? Fluid may ask you to create or import your wallet here once — it stays on this phone. Lille never sees what you type inside Fluid.
Your Fluid wallet, inside Lille. Lille never sees what you type here — this window is a plain container, and Fluid\'s keys stay Fluid\'s.
Her own agentic wallet — separate from your Fluid wallet. She spends only from it, within caps you set, and only with your approval unless you switch autonomy on.

This is Lille\'s own wallet — the agentic wallet from her design: her own keys, generated on this phone and kept in her encrypted vault, completely separate from your Fluid wallet. Fund it only with what she may spend. She can never touch your Fluid wallet; the most she can ever hold is what you send here.
Her address — send funds here to fund her:

Funding is the one step that happens wherever your money already is: send any amount to her address from Fluid or anywhere else. Everything after that — balances, sends, approvals — happens here, inside Lille.
Return funds to my Fluid wallet

Defaults are $5 per transaction and $20 per day. Raise them to anything, or switch a cap off — whatever you set is enforced by her signer itself, not by her good behaviour. Prepare-and-ask stays the rule until you switch autonomy on below.
Warning: with a cap off, that limit is gone — her wallet\'s balance is the only limit left on that axis.
Let Lille spend within these caps without asking each time
Share your personal invite link. When a friend installs Lille and signs in with their own name, your invite counts. A friend can only ever count for one inviter — the first inviter wins.
Use Lille on two phones? Export your invite list here and import it on the other phone to keep your count in step.

Lille works fully with no key at all — the free keyless brain is her default. If you have your OWN free key from one of these services, adding it gives her one more brain route to fall back to when the free routes are busy. A key is stored only on this phone, in her encrypted vault; it is sent only to that service, never shown, never logged. Adding or removing a key is always your choice, and she never asks for one.
Automatic, encrypted backup of your chats, tasks and Lille\'s vault — locked by your Fluid wallet, restorable on a new phone.

Your backup is a locked file only your Fluid wallet can open. Lille seals your chats, tasks and her vault into it automatically — to a folder on this phone, and (if you consent) to your own Google Drive. Google stores the lock-box, never the key. No Fluid wallet, no restore — ever: the key is your wallet\'s signature, and nobody else can produce it.
Include my browser logins in the backup
A browser login (like your X session) inside a backup is a logged-in account in a file — sealed with the same encryption, but only turn this on if you want those sessions to survive a phone switch.
Forget backup key on this phone
